newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's TCorp sees A$4.9 bln funding need.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's TCorp sees A$4.9 bln funding need.

text.p: The New South Wales government's borrowing arm Treasury Corp (TCorp) said on Wednesday that its total funding requirement for 1997/98 would be A$4.9 billion.
"Total funding requirement for 1997/98 of A$4.9 billion is higher than the 1996/97 level, largely due to a higher level of A$4.6 billion in maturing debt," TCorp said in a statement.
The A$4.9 billion funding requirement consisted of the A$4.6 billion in maturing debt, A$400 million in Federal debt refinancing and then minus A$100 million in client net funding.

The 1997/98 funding requirement compared with a funding requirement in 1996/97 of A$3.9 billion and A$8.3 billion in 1995/96. In 1996/97 maturing borrowings totalled A$4.2 billion and client net funding was A$700 million.
TCorp said its funding strategy would be similar to that set in 1996/97.
"Total domestic benchmark bonds on issue will be targetted to average at least A$12 billion over the course of the year, with targetted minimum volume for each hot stock of A$1 billion," it said.
The major focus for the domestic programme over the coming year would be to build up the outstanding number of 2006 and 2008 bonds.
TCorp also said it would continue to access offshore markets for 40-50 percent of its total term funding requirements.

"The Japanese retail investor market and the Euro-A$ market are expected to provide the main funding opportunities again in 1997/98, though other offshore sources will be tapped if they prove to be cost effective."
TCorp said it had established commercial paper programmes in excess of US$6 billion, but these programmes had been dormant for the past 18 months.
"Issuance under these programmes may be reactivated during 1997/98 if the traditional sources of offshore funding cease to be cost effective," it said.
